 Two McPherson residents, 6-year-old Cole Adrian and 35-year-old Nick Shafer, died in the crash. 
 By Jordan Tovar Published : Nov. 13, 2026 at 12:04 AM CST | Updated : 9 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google McPHERSON, Kan. — Nearly a month after a deadly crash at Stryker Sports Complex, some McPherson residents hope the decision not to file criminal charges against the pickup’s driver will give their community a chance to heal.
 Cole Adrian, 6, and Nick Shafer, 35, both of McPherson, died in the crash. Sedgwick County District Attorney Marc Bennett announced Thursday that the woman driving the pickup would not face criminal charges .
 Photo of 6-year-old Cole Adrian, killed in a crash on Oct. 17, 2026, at Wichita's Stryker Sports Complex (Family of Cole Adrian -- Obituary image published by Stockham Family Funeral Home) Photo of Nicholas Schafer, a 35-year-old McPherson man who died after being hit by a pickup on Oct. 17 at Wichita's Stryker Sports Complex (Family of Nicholas Schafer, used for his obituary) Cindy and John Krehbiel, who live in McPherson, described the outpouring of support for families affected by the crash, including money raised to help them.
 “The community has really rallied around them,” one of the Krehbiels said. “There’s been lots of money raised for the families affected.”
 Cindy Krehbiel said community members want to help without seeking recognition. 
 “They just want to pitch in and help these people get through this horrible thing,” she said.
 A GoFundMe has been set up to help the family of a Nick Schafer. Several fundraisers have taken place in Wichita and McPherson, you can find them all here .
